evidence: Don. p. 1744 P. (Lewis & Short s.v. dēminūtīvus)
terms.comment: The later grammarians’ word, also nōmen dēminūtīvum (Traupman 246). Quintilian says dēminūtum and speaks of dēminūtiō, the forming of diminutives: fūniculus shows that fūnis is masculine.

evidence: Quint. 1.5.46: quia prō nōmine integrō positum sit dēminūtum

phrases.latin: dēminūtiō genus modo dētegit, et, nē ab eōdem exemplō recēdam, fūnem masculīnum esse fūniculus ostendit
phrases.english: the diminutive form sometimes reveals the gender: to keep to the same example, fūniculus shows that fūnis is masculine

sources: Lewis & Short: deminutivus · Lewis & Short: deminuo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 246.
